articleTitle: IEE Colloquium on 'Land Mobile Satellite Systems' (Digest No.154)
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Land Mobile Satellite Systems
IEE Colloquium on Land Mobile Satellite Systems
abstract: This paper proposes a space segment which provides GSM (Global Standard for Mobile communications) compatible mobile communications in the European region. The system will use a three-satellite TUNDRA orbit constellation of eccentricity 0.15. BLQS-CDMA is the proposed access method. A circularly symmetric 7 spotbeam coverage of Europe is proposed. The system architecture and protocols allow compatibility with the GSM system. Voice, paging and low rate data services can be provided to subscribers across Eastern and Western Europe, including maritime areas. Terminal costs are minimised to aid market penetration. System capacity calculations suggest that up to 200000 subscribers could be supported by the system on a GSM compatible channel rate of 11.4 kbit/s.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: The current state of land mobile satellite systems
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Land Mobile Satellite Systems
abstract: This paper provides a review of the current status of land mobile satellite systems throughout the world as a basis for the remainder of the colloquium. It addresses the key technical issues relating to land mobile satellite systems, and concludes with a status report on the development of the major operational and proposed systems.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Land Mobile Satellite Systems
abstract: The European Space Agency is developing the EMS payload to be embarked on the ITALSAT-2 satellite due for launch by the end of 1992. The associated communications systems PRODAT-2 and MSBN (Mobile Satellite Business Network) are described.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Frequency reuse in land mobile-satellite systems
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Land Mobile Satellite Systems
abstract: The author reviews the current methods of re-using the radio spectrum in the land mobile satellite service (LMSS) using satellites in the geostationary satellite orbit. The methods described relate to the performance of the satellite and mobile antennas. It is acknowledged that the satellite antenna provides a good method of frequency reuse through the use of multiple spot beams. However, when two or more satellite systems plan to provide services to the same geographical area, the mobile antenna plays an important part in facilitating sharing of frequencies. Developments in mobile Earth station design are lead to use of directional antennas combined with an antenna tracking mechanism. It is proposed that their lower sidelobe gain be used to protect other co-frequency LMSS operations, recognising also a requirement for sufficient orbital separation of the satellites.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Low Earth orbit mobile satellite systems at 20/30 GHz
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Land Mobile Satellite Systems
abstract: A perceived lack of spectrum at the lower frequency bands arises due to unfavourable comparison between the spectrum utilization of terrestrial cellular mobile systems and satellite mobile. Advances in millimetre RE technology from both civil and military R&D programmes have produced devices and systems which make 20/30 GHz satellite mobile concepts feasible and offer some interesting advantages over lower frequency systems.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Land Mobile Satellite Systems
abstract: The author provides a short overview of the current land mobile systems, and those about to be introduced, as well as future systems. Many of the systems described are also used by maritime users, and separate systems have been developed for aeronautical use. A technical summary of the various Inmarsat land mobile systems is given in a table.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Characterisation of the high elevation orbit satellite-mobile radio channel at L and S bands
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Land Mobile Satellite Systems
abstract: Advances in spacecraft technology have made feasible the use of large constellations of low earth orbiting (LEO) spacecraft. The 1.5 GHz (L-band), and 2.5 GHz (S-band) regions of the spectrum had been expected to be the most likely frequencies allocated for such services. The present paper reports the progress of a collaborative research project set-up between the University, the UK-Radiocommunications Agency and the European Space Agency (ESA-ESTEC), to obtain propagation information relevant to these systems.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: EUTELTRACS: the European land mobile satellite service
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Land Mobile Satellite Systems
abstract: Applying the mobile communications expertise of ALCATEL QUALCOMM under the overall network operation of the European Telecommunications Satellite Organization, EUTELTRACS provides an integrated message exchange and position reporting service for the European transportation industry with the aim of increasing cost-effectiveness, radically improving efficiency and security, and enhancing business flexibility. This paper describes the architecture of the system, the message exchange and position reporting service, and gives an overview of the commercial deployment of EUTELTRACS and of the current regulatory situation for its operation within Europe.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A trellis coded 16-QAM modem for land mobile communications
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Land Mobile Satellite Systems
abstract: The performance of low bit rate (10.8 Kb/s) 8-PSK and trellis coded modulation (TCM) 16-QAM modems operating over a Rician fading land mobile satellite channel is evaluated and compared. Considerable TCM coding gain is obtained with the aid of a pilot symbol sequence, which allows successful coherent detection under severe fading, and diversity in time by interleaving using several multiplexed TCM codecs. The proposed modem is well suited for fully digital implementation.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A digital signal processing payload concept for land mobile satellite communications
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Land Mobile Satellite Systems
abstract: The paper summarises system tradeoff aspects of studies performed for ESA into the feasibility of an advanced processing payload concept, based in particular on the use of digital beamforming techniques. The baseline system described has resulted from extensive tradeoffs between a number of candidate payload and system configuration options.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>
